title: Centralized Audit Trail for Distributed Microservices
business: A fintech startup running distributed microservices across multiple Google Cloud projects needs to maintain a unified audit trail for compliance and troubleshooting.
problem: Logs are scattered across individual service instances, making it impossible to reconstruct transaction flows or identify the root cause of intermittent service failures.
solution: Google Cloud Logging provides a centralized platform to collect, search, analyze, and route logs from all Google Cloud resources and applications into a single, searchable interface.
steps: Enable the Logging API across all project resources to ensure logs are captured.
Configure log sinks to aggregate logs from various services into a centralized Log Bucket.
Define exclusion filters to manage log volume and focus on critical audit events.
Use the Logs Explorer to perform complex queries and analyze cross-service request patterns.
outcome: The engineering team gains a unified view of system behavior, enabling rapid identification of failures and simplified compliance reporting.
limitation: High-volume logging can lead to increased storage costs and potential latency in log availability; check the ingestion rates and storage usage in the Monitoring dashboard to manage this tradeoff.

The cost of running microservices is too high for the startup.
